from datetime import datetime, timezone


def _parse_updated_at(text):
    """Parse an ISO 8601 timestamp into a timezone-aware datetime."""
    text = text.strip()
    # Python < 3.11 does not accept a trailing "Z" in fromisoformat.
    if text.endswith(("Z", "z")):
        text = text[:-1] + "+00:00"
    dt = datetime.fromisoformat(text)
    if dt.tzinfo is None:
        # No offset given; assume UTC so comparisons still work.
        dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    return dt


def merge_attendance(records):
    """Keep one record per (player, date): the most recently updated one.

    Timestamps are compared as actual instants in time, so different UTC
    offsets are handled correctly. If two records for the same player and
    date have the same instant, the one appearing later in the list wins
    (it was uploaded later). Output order follows the first appearance of
    each (player, date) pair in the input.
    """
    best = {}  # (player, date) -> (parsed updated_at, record)
    for record in records:
        key = (record["player"], record["date"])
        updated = _parse_updated_at(record["updated_at"])
        current = best.get(key)
        if current is None or updated >= current[0]:
            best[key] = (updated, record)
    return [record for _, record in best.values()]
